findings.reason: the node cannot satisfy the section as written; the mechanism has to be keyed on the lane (a declared modality, which is §1's and §7's own principle that a declaration claims a measured delivery) rather than on "a dialect with no attach flag", and saying so changes both the Change paragraph and the test it names.
findings.text: §14 says "for a dialect with no attach flag, it appends to the prompt each attached image's path … and the dialect's `argv` stops refusing the images", but the claude lane and the clive lane are the same dialect: `_CliveDialect(_ClaudeDialect)` at `reckon/_backends.py:2006` overrides only `subscription_login`, it carries no `name` of its own (so `_CliveDialect().name == 'claude'`, inherited from `reckon/_backends.py:1577`), and `_refuse_images` has exactly one call site, in the shared `_ClaudeDialect.argv` at `reckon/_backends.py:1594`; there is also no per-backend marker anywhere that reports whether a dialect has an attach flag. So a change keyed on the dialect stops the `claude` parametrisation of `test_a_lane_that_cannot_carry_the_figure_refuses_by_name` (`tests/test_launch_plan_attaches_images.py:105`) refusing too, which is exactly what the done-when at line 266 forbids ("that test's other lanes still refuse").

findings.reason: the claim motivates where figure reviews should run, not how the section's mechanism works; §14's change, measure and control all stand without it, so removing or citing it alters no deliverable.
findings.text: §14 rests its reason for moving figure reviews off codex on "On 2026-10-20 a peer reported that codex read-only reviews fail on this fleet node on `bwrap: Can't mkdir /tmp/.git`" and "the lead's codex lift is for high-level work only", neither of which resolves to any file, plan, section or commit in the repository, so a later reader cannot confirm the routing rationale this section states.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — §14 grounds its routing rationale on an anchor no reader can open.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §14's done-when is measurable (a `launch_plan` on clive given one image carries a prompt naming the path and no longer raises; the project layer with an empty host layer declares image on clive as well as codex) and it declares a negative control whose failure is stated in terms of the guard ("with the image naming removed from `launch_plan`, the launch prompt names no image and the test fails").
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §14 keeps every log under the run directory with a revision header, a literal command and a trailing `EXIT=`, which survives the run and is the same convention §6 and §10 through §13 already use.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §14 introduces no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag: the names it adds (`_refuse_images`, `launch_plan`, `stdin_text`, `input_modalities`) are mechanism names, and its prose describes what changes rather than a changelog of what changed.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §14's stated mechanism is written at dialect granularity while its own done-when requires lane granularity, and claude and clive are one dialect object, so the mechanism as written cannot produce the measure.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — the change and the declaration are one goal, a local lane that can be handed a figure it can see, and the plan's own §7 bundles a measured delivery with the declaration it earns.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — `plan-section-depends-on` carries `s14 -> a-review-can-see-the-figure#s13`, which is the section §14 measures from, and the sections §14 also leans on (§10's run-local PNGs, §12's lane selection) are already declared `done`.
